Rashi on Gittin 26a:10:1.hebrew: דקתני אין כותבין - והדר תנא כתבו על המחובר כשר, ומדקשיא רישא לסיפא, אוקימנא דהכי קאמר: אין כותבין טופס, שמא יכתוב תורף כו':
Rashi on Gittin 26a:10:1.english: As [it] teaches: "One may not write" - And then it teaches: [If] one wrote it on something attached [to the ground, it is] valid; and since the first clause contradicts the latter clause, we established that this is what it is saying: One may not write the standard form [of the bill of divorce], lest one [come to] write the essential details, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:11:1.hebrew: אבל סיפא - "הכל כשרין לכתוב", דקתני "שאין קיום הגט אלא בחותמיו":
Rashi on Gittin 26a:11:1.english: However, [in] the latter clause - [this refers to the Mishnah beginning] "Everyone is fit to write [a bill of divorce]," which teaches, "for the ratification of a bill of divorce is only through its signatories":

Rashi on Gittin 26a:11:2.hebrew: אימא ר' מאיר היא - ואינו צריך לשייר מקום התורף, ואשמעינן שמואל דצריך, ורבי אלעזר היא. וסיפא דקתני "שאין קיום הגט אלא בחותמיו", לאו לאכשורי תורף דחרש שוטה וקטן דשלא לשמה קאי, אלא אמציעתא קאי: "האשה כותבת את גיטה" — לשמה — "והאיש כותב את שוברו", שאין קיום הגט אלא במסירתו ולא בחתימתו. והא דנקט "חותמיו" — משום דרוב עדי מסירה הם החתומים בו, ורוב גיטין חתומים הם אפי' לר"א, מפני תיקון העולם:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:11:2.english: One could say that it is [the view of] Rabbi Meir - and one does not need to leave the place of the essential part [of the bill of divorce] blank. And Shmuel teaches us that one does need [to leave it blank], and [the Mishnah] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar. And the latter clause, which teaches "for the ratification of a bill of divorce is only through its signatories," does not refer to validating the essential part [written by] a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor — which is not [written] for her own sake — rather, it refers to the middle clause: "The woman writes her bill of divorce" — [meaning] for her own sake — "and the man [writes] his receipt," for the ratification of a bill of divorce is only through its delivery, and not through its signing. And the reason [the Mishnah] states "its signatories" is because most witnesses of delivery are the ones who are signed on it, and most bills of divorce are signed even according to Rabbi Elazar, for the betterment of the world:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:1.hebrew: איכא לאוקמא כר' אלעזר - ולא קשיא מידי, כדפרישית:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:1.english: It can be interpreted in accordance with Rabbi Elazar - And there is no difficulty at all, as I have explained.

Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:2.hebrew: אבל הא מדסיפא - פליג ר' אלעזר ארישא, דקתני: "רבי אלעזר מכשיר בכולן חוץ מגיטי נשים", ורישא מכשיר אף בגיטי נשים:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:2.english: But [regarding] this [mishna], since the latter clause - Rabbi Elazar disagrees with the first clause, as [the mishna] teaches: "Rabbi Elazar validates [them] in all [documents] except for bills of divorce," whereas the first clause validates [them] even in bills of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:3.hebrew: אימא רישא לאו רבי אלעזר היא - וא"צ לשייר מקום "הרי את מותרת", אלא מקום השמות לבדן, משום קטטה כדלקמן:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:3.english: Say [that] the first clause is not [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar - and it is not necessary to leave [blank] the place of "Behold, you are permitted [to any man]," but rather only the place of the names alone, because of [the concern for] a quarrel, as [explained] below:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:4.hebrew: קמ"ל - שמואל, דרישא נמי כר"א, ותרי תנאי ואליבא דר' אלעזר, כדלקמיה:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:12:4.english: [He] teaches us - [that is,] Shmuel [teaches us], that the first clause is also in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, and [that there are] two Tannaim according to [the view of] Rabbi Elazar, as [explained] below:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:13:1.english: Due to the ordinance of a scribe - [The Sages] permitted writing [the] standard part [of the document] not for her sake:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:13:2.hebrew: ור"א היא - הא דקתני "מפני התקנה" התירו לכתוב טופס, הא לאו הכי הוה אסיר — רבי אלעזר היא, דבעי לשמה בכתיבה מדאורייתא:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:13:2.english: And it is [the view of] Rabbi Elazar - That which [the Mishnah] teaches, "due to the ordinance" [they] permitted writing the standard part [in advance], [whereas] otherwise it would be forbidden — [this] is [the view of] Rabbi Elazar, who requires [that it be written] for her sake in the writing [itself] by Torah law:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:13:3.hebrew: לא לכתוב - דלמא אתי למכתב תורף, אלא משום תקנת סופר, שיהו מזומנין לו, שרו ליה, ובלבד שישייר תורף לכתוב לשמה; ותורף דשאר שטרות נמי גזר משום תורף דגיטין:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:13:3.english: [He should] not write - lest he come to write the essential part [as well]; rather, due to the ordinance [for the benefit] of a scribe, so that [the documents] be readily available for him, they permitted [writing the standard part] to him, provided that he leaves out the essential part to write [it] for her sake. And [regarding] the essential part of other documents as well, [the Sages] decreed [against writing it in advance] because of the essential part of bills of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:14:1.hebrew: ורבי יהודה כו' - וגזר שטרות, אפי' טופס, אטו גיטין:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:14:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, etc. - And he decreed [regarding] documents, even the standard part [tofes], due to bills of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:14:2.hebrew: שטרות אטו גיטין - בטופס לא גזר, דגזירה לגזירה היא:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:14:2.english: [He decreed] documents due to bills of divorce - Regarding the standard part [tofes of other documents], he did not decree [invalidation], because it is a decree upon a decree:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:16:1.hebrew: והא כי כתיב לה אתורף כתיב - דבקרא כריתות כתיב, דהיינו תורף, והיכי יליף ר"א מיניה למיסר טופס:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:16:1.english: But when "for her" is written, it is written regarding the essential part - For in the verse, "severance" is written, which is the essential part, so how does Rabbi Elazar derive from it to prohibit [pre-writing] the standard part?

Rashi on Gittin 26a:17:1.hebrew: אלא - לא תימא "שנאמר", דמשמע מיניה יליף, אלא "משום", כלומר: משום שנאמר בתורף "וכתב לה" לשמה, גזרינן טופס אטו תורף דאורייתא:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:17:1.english: Rather - do not say [merely] "that it is stated," which implies that he derives [it directly] from there, but rather "because," meaning: because it is stated regarding the essential part [of the bill of divorce], "and he writes for her" — for her sake — we decree [this requirement for] the standard part on account of the essential part, [which is] a biblical [requirement]:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:1:1.hebrew: לא רצה אינה מקודשת - דלא בעל אלא על תנאי ולא נתקיים, וכי רצה מיהא מקודשת, ואע"ג דמשעת בעילה ספק רוצה ספק אינו רוצה, אמרינן הוברר דמשעת בעילה הוו קידושין:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:1:1.english: [If the father] does not desire [it], she is not betrothed - because he only engaged in intercourse on a condition, and [the condition] was not fulfilled. However, when [the father] does desire [it], she is betrothed, and even though at the time of intercourse it is uncertain whether he desires [it] or does not desire [it], we say it is [retroactively] clarified that from the time of intercourse it was a [valid] betrothal:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:3:1.english: Untithed produce retroactively - for the terumah was never clarified:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:3:2.hebrew: לכשיבקע - כשיבא לידי כך, ודאי טבלים שתה, אבל אין לחוש לכך, דלא שכיח ליבקע:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:3:2.english: When it bursts - When it comes to that, he will certainly have drunk tevel [untithed produce], but one need not be concerned about this, because it is uncommon for it to burst:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:4:1.hebrew: הכותב טופסי גיטין - שסופר הוא ונוטל שכר, ורוצה שיהו מזומנין לו, פעמים שאדם בא לשוכרו והוא טרוד בשטרות אחרים:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:4:1.english: One who writes the standard texts of bills of divorce - [That is, one] who is a scribe and takes a fee, and wants them to be ready at hand for him, [for] sometimes a person comes to hire him while he is busy with other documents:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:4:2.hebrew: צריך שיניח מקום האיש וכו' - שאם רואה תגר ביניהם, לא יאמר "הריני כותב כל הגט", ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:4:2.english: He must leave [blank] the place of the man, etc. - For if [the scribe] sees a quarrel between them [a husband and wife], he should not say, "Behold, I will write the entire bill of divorce [in advance]"; and in the Gemara, it explains the reason:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:4:3.hebrew: צריך שיניח מקום כו' - ואם שמע הסופר שהיה אחד רודף אחר חבירו להלוותו מנה, לא יאמר: "הריני כותב מיד, ואניח מקום הזמן לבדו שלא יהא שטר מוקדם", אלא צריך שיניח מקום הלוה והמלוה והמעות, אע"ג דליכא למיחש למידי — גזירה שטרות אטו גיטין:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:4:3.english: He must leave [blank] the place, etc. - And if [the scribe] heard that one [person] was pursuing his fellow to lend him a maneh, he should not say: "I will write [the document] immediately and leave [blank] the place for the date alone, so that it will not be a predated document"; rather, he must leave [blank] the place for the borrower, and the lender, and the [amount of] money, even though there is nothing to be concerned about — [as] a decree [concerning] loan documents on account of bills of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:6:1.hebrew: מפני התקנה - בגמ' מפרש אהיכא קאי:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:6:1.english: Due to the ordinance - In the Gemara, it explains to what [this] refers:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:7:1.hebrew: פוסל בכולן - ואפילו הניח מקומות הללו, וטעמא מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Gittin 26a:7:1.english: [Rabbi Yehuda] invalidates all of them - Even if he left these spaces [blank], and the reason is explained in the Gemara:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:7:2.hebrew: ר' אלעזר מכשיר בכולן - ובלבד שיניח מקומות הללו:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:7:2.english: Rabbi Elazar deems all of them valid - provided that he leaves these spaces [blank]:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:7:3.english: Except for bills of divorce - because with respect to them, we make a decree [prohibiting writing] the standard part [tofes] on account of the essential part [toref]:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:7:4.hebrew: שנאמר וכתב לה - בגמרא פריך: האי אתורף הוא דכתיב:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:7:4.english: As it is stated: “And he writes for her” - In the Gemara, it raises a difficulty: This [verse] is written regarding the toref [the essential part of the bill of divorce]:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:8:1.english: Also the place of "You are hereby permitted" - for this too is [part of] the essence of a bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:8:2.hebrew: עדי מסירה כרתי - הלכך "וכתב לה" לאו אחתימה קאי, דחתימת עדים אינה אלא מדברי סופרים מפני תיקון העולם; וכי כתיב "וכתב לה", משמע אעיקר כריתות קאי, דהיינו כל הני דאמרן:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:8:2.english: Witnesses of the transmission effect [the divorce] - Therefore, "and he writes for her" does not refer to the signing [of the witnesses], for the signing of witnesses is only by Rabbinic enactment for the betterment of the world; and when it is written "and he writes for her," it means it refers to the essence of [the document of] severance, which is all these [parts] that we mentioned:

Rashi on Gittin 26a:9:1.hebrew: וצריכא - לשמואל לאוקמי להני תלת סתמי כר"א, ולמימרא בכולהו "והוא ששייר מקום התורף": "אין כותבין על המחובר" (לעיל גיטין דף כא:), "והכל כשרין לכתוב" (לעיל גיטין כב:), "והכותב טופסי גיטין" — כולהו אוקמינהו שמואל כר"א:
Rashi on Gittin 26a:9:1.english: And it is necessary - for Shmuel to establish these three anonymous [Mishnayot] in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, and to state regarding all of them, "provided that he left [blank] the place of the essential part [of the document]": "One may not write on that which is attached [to the ground]" (above, Gittin 21b), "And all are fit to write [a bill of divorce]" (above, Gittin 22b), [and] "One who writes standard forms of bills of divorce" — Shmuel established all of them in accordance with Rabbi Elazar:

Tosafot on Gittin 26a:11:1.hebrew: אבל סיפא דקתני שאין קיום הגט אלא בחותמיו אימא ר"מ היא - תימה, דבסוף פרק שני לעיל (גיטין דף כג.) מוקי לה ר' זריקא א"ר יוחנן כר"מ, ופריך עלה מההיא דמחובר, דאמר רבה בר בר חנה א"ר יוחנן: ר"א היא, ודחק לשנויי: אמוראי נינהו אליבא דר' יוחנן. ומאי קושיא? הא משמע הכא דאע"ג דמוקמינן ההיא דמחובר כר"א, מ"מ מוקמינן שפיר ההיא ד"הכל כשרים" כר"מ! ואור"י, דאע"פ שעושה צריכותא בזה, מ"מ מיסתבר דאתיא כחד תנא. אבל הך דפירקין, ודאי ר' יוחנן מוקי לה כר"מ, משום טעמא דמסיק: מדסיפא ר"א, רישא לאו ר"א; דמטעם זה קאמר ר"י בפרק ד' אחין (יבמות דף כז:): "אחיות איני יודע מי שנאן". ועוד, דבתרתי קמייתא דמתניין בחדא פירקא איכא קפידא טפי לאוקמינהו כחד תנא:
Tosafot on Gittin 26a:11:1.english: However, the latter clause, which teaches that the ratification of a bill of divorce is only through its signatories, say that it is Rabbi Meir - This is surprising, for at the end of the second chapter above (Gittin 23a), Rabbi Zerika in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan establishes it as [following] Rabbi Meir, and [the Gemara] objects to it from that [mishna] concerning [something] attached [to the ground], where Rabbah bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: It is Rabbi Elazar, and [the Gemara] was forced to answer: They are Amoraim [disagreeing] according to Rabbi Yoḥanan. But what is the difficulty? Behold, it is implied here that even though we establish that [mishna] of [something] attached as Rabbi Elazar, nevertheless we can properly establish that [mishna] of "All are fit" as Rabbi Meir! And Rabbeinu Yitzḥak says that even though [the Gemara] makes a distinction of necessity in this [case], nevertheless it is reasonable that [they both] follow one Tanna. However, [as for] this [mishna] of our chapter, Rabbi Yoḥanan certainly establishes it as Rabbi Meir because of the reason that [the Gemara] concludes: since the latter clause is Rabbi Elazar, the former clause is not Rabbi Elazar; for from this [very] reason Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Aḥin (Yevamot 27b): "[Regarding the mishna of] sisters, I do not know who taught them." And furthermore, regarding the first two [mishnayot] that are taught in one chapter, there is greater insistence to establish them as [following] one Tanna:

Tosafot on Gittin 26a:13:1.hebrew: מפני התקנה מאי מפני התקנה - מקום הזמן דתנא ברישא, דקבע בגמרא אחר כך, היינו משום דאתא לפרושי "מפני התקנה" אליבא דמאן דמוקי לה כר"א, דאין פירושו כמו למאן דמוקי לה כר"מ:
Tosafot on Gittin 26a:13:1.english: Due to the ordinance; what [is] "due to the ordinance" - [As for] "the space for the date," which [the Mishnah] taught earlier, [and] which [the Gemara] placed in the Gemara afterwards — this is because [the Gemara] came to explain "due to the ordinance" according to the one who establishes [the Mishnah] as Rabbi Elazar, since its explanation [according to him] is not the same as [it is] according to the one who establishes it as Rabbi Meir:

Tosafot on Gittin 26a:2:1.hebrew: בין לרבי יהודה בין לר"ש לא שנא וכו' - ורב יוסף דמסיק בפ' בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לז:) דלר"ש לית ליה ברירה, גבי "הריני מערב לשבתות של כל השנה כולה, רציתי אלך, רציתי לא אלך", דמסיק רב יוסף: איפוך, ולר"ש רצה מבעוד יום עירובו עירוב כו' — רב יוסף יחלק בין בתולה בדעת עצמו לתולה בדעת אחרים:
Tosafot on Gittin 26a:2:1.english: Whether according to Rabbi Yehuda or according to Rabbi Shimon, it is no different, etc. - And [as for] Rav Yosef, who concludes in the chapter [entitled] Bekhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 37b) that according to Rabbi Shimon he does not hold of [retroactive] clarification — regarding [the Mishnah]: "Behold, I am making an eruv for the Sabbaths of the entire year: [if] I want, I will go; [if] I want, I will not go," where Rav Yosef concludes: "Reverse [it], and according to Rabbi Shimon, [only if] he wanted while it was still day is his eruv an eruv, etc." — Rav Yosef would distinguish between making [it] dependent on one's own decision and making [it] dependent on the decision of others:

Tosafot on Gittin 26a:3:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא כו' - בפרק בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לז:) מפרש רבא טעמא משום דבעינן ראשית ששיריה ניכרין. ונראה דהתם גריס "רבה", מדאיירי אביי בתריה; ועוד, דהתם נמי מסיק טעמא כי הכא:
Tosafot on Gittin 26a:3:1.english: There, [it is] as the reason is taught, etc. - In the chapter [entitled] Bekhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 37b), Rava explains the reason [is] because we require a "first" [portion] whose remainder is discernible. And it appears that there the reading is "Rabbah," since Abaye discusses [it] after him; and furthermore, there too it concludes [with] the reason like here:

Tosafot on Gittin 26a:7:1.hebrew: רבי אלעזר מכשיר בכולן - פירש בקונטרס: ובלבד שיניח מקומות הללו. וקשה לר"י, דבגמרא פסיק רב כר' אלעזר וקאמר: אפי' בשטרות? והאמר רב פפי כו', אלמא מחזי כשיקרא, ה"נ מחזי כשיקרא! ואי לא מכשיר ר"א אלא בטופס דשטרות, מה מחזי כשיקרא איכא, מאחר שהניח מקום המלוה והלוה והמעות? ועוד, משמע דלא פריך מדרב פפי אלא משום דפסיק כר' אלעזר, אבל אי הוה סבר כרבנן הוה ניחא ליה; ואי שייך בטופס מחזי כשיקרא, אפי' סבר כרבנן תקשי לרב פפי! ונראה לר"י דר"א מכשיר בשטרות אפי' תורף, והשתא מיחזי כשיקרא, שכותב "פלוני לוה מפלוני" ועדיין לא לוה. "חוץ מגיטי נשים" — דפסיל אפילו טופס, מדקתני "משום שנאמר וכתב לה", משמע דפסיל בגיטי נשים טפי מת"ק. וא"ת: ומנא ליה לגמרא דר"א מכשיר בשטרות אפי' תורף, דפריך מדרב פפי? דלמא בטופס דשטרות דווקא מכשיר! וי"ל: דאם איתא דלא מכשיר אלא בטופס, היה לו לקבוע דברי ר"א אחר ת"ק, והיה לו לקצר ולשנות "ר' אלעזר פוסל בגיטי נשים ור' יהודה פוסל בכולן", וגם היה ראוי לשנות בסדר זה שכל אחד מחמיר משלפניו. אבל אי רבי אלעזר אתא לאכשורי בשטרות אפי' תורף, ניחא דתנא דברי רבי יהודה קודם, משום דקאי את"ק דאיירי בטופס, ור"א בשטרות מכשיר טפי מתנא קמא ובגיטין פסיל טפי:
Tosafot on Gittin 26a:7:1.english: Rabbi Elazar deems all of them valid - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: provided that he leaves [blank] these places [i.e., the specific details]. And this is difficult for the Ri: for in the Gemara, Rav rules in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, and [the Gemara] asks: Even for [loan] documents? But did Rav Pappi not say, etc. — thus it looks like a falsehood; here too it looks like a falsehood! Now, if Rabbi Elazar only deems valid the standard part [tofes] of [loan] documents, what appearance of falsehood is there, since he left [blank] the place of the lender, the borrower, and the amount of money? Furthermore, it is implied that [the Gemara] only challenges [Rav] from [the statement of] Rav Pappi because he ruled in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, whereas if he had held in accordance with the Rabbis, it would have been fine for it; yet if the appearance of falsehood applies to the standard part, even if he held in accordance with the Rabbis, [the ruling] would be difficult according to Rav Pappi! Rather, it appears to the Ri that Rabbi Elazar deems valid in [loan] documents even the essential part [toref], and now it looks like a falsehood, because he writes "So-and-so borrowed from so-and-so" when he has not yet borrowed. "Except for bills of divorce" — for he invalidates even the standard part; from the fact that [the Mishnah] teaches "because it is stated: And he writes for her," it is implied that he is more stringent in invalidating bills of divorce than the first Tanna. And if you say: From where does the Gemara know that Rabbi Elazar deems valid in [loan] documents even the essential part, such that it challenges [Rav] from [the statement of] Rav Pappi? Perhaps he only deems valid the standard part of [loan] documents! And one can answer: If it were true that he only deems valid the standard part, [the Tanna] should have placed the words of Rabbi Elazar after the first Tanna, and he should have been concise and taught: "Rabbi Elazar invalidates bills of divorce, and Rabbi Yehuda invalidates all of them"; and it would also have been fitting to teach in this order, so that each one is more stringent than the one before him. However, if Rabbi Elazar comes to deem valid in [loan] documents even the essential part, it is understandable why [the Tanna] taught the words of Rabbi Yehuda first: because [Rabbi Yehuda] is addressing the first Tanna, who is speaking of the standard part, whereas Rabbi Elazar is more lenient than the first Tanna regarding [loan] documents and more stringent regarding bills of divorce:

Tosafot on Gittin 26a:7:2.hebrew: חוץ מגיטי נשים - ואין לומר בשחרורי עבדים נמי פסיל, דאם כן, בפ"ק (לעיל גיטין ט.) גבי שלשה דברים ששוו גיטי נשים לשחרורי עבדים, ליתני "וכדברי ר"א בארבע", כדקתני "וכדברי ר"מ בארבע":
Tosafot on Gittin 26a:7:2.english: Except for bills of divorce - And one cannot say [that] he also invalidates [it] in [the case of] bills of manumission of slaves, for if so, in the first chapter (above, Gittin 9a), regarding [the statement] "Three matters in which women's bills of divorce are equal to bills of manumission of slaves," it should have taught "and according to the words of Rabbi Elazar, in four," just as it teaches "and according to the words of Rabbi Meir, in four":

Tosafot on Gittin 26a:8:1.hebrew: וצריך שיניח מקום הרי את מותרת לכל אדם - בכל דוכתי משמע שכותבין לשון זה בגט, ובפ' בתרא (לקמן גיטין פה.) נמי תניא: גופו של גט "הרי את מותרת לכל אדם". והנהיג ר"ת לכתוב לשון זה בגט, אבל בטופסי גיטין לא היה כתוב. ומ"מ אין להוציא לעז על גיטין הראשונים, שהרי מאריכין לכתוב כמה לשונות בגט, דחשיב כמו "הרי את מותרת לכל אדם":
Tosafot on Gittin 26a:8:1.english: And he must leave the space for "You are hereby permitted to any man" - Everywhere it is implied that we write this wording in a bill of divorce, and in the last chapter (later, Gittin 85a) it is also taught: The essential part of a bill of divorce is "You are hereby permitted to any man." And Rabbeinu Tam instituted [the practice of] writing this wording in a bill of divorce, whereas in the [earlier] standard formularies of bills of divorce it was not written. Nevertheless, one should not cast aspersions on the earlier bills of divorce, for they write at length several expressions in the bill of divorce, which is considered like "You are hereby permitted to any man":
